observations: Photo 0 shows a Sigma zoom lens with focal lengths 12, 15, 17, 20, and 24mm marked on the zoom ring.
The lens has an AF/M switch and a distance scale window.
Photo 1 shows the front element and the text '12-24mm 1:4.5-5.6 II DG HSM' on the barrel.
Photo 2 shows the serial number 1016378 and 'LENS MADE IN JAPAN'.
The lens has a built-in petal-shaped lens hood.
The exterior finish appears clean with no obvious peeling or heavy wear.
All photos contain a watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI IKE STEPHEN'.

claims.evidence: The rear mount is not shown in any photo to confirm it is the Canon EF version.
The barrel and rubber rings in photos 0 and 2 show very little wear.
Lenses do not have shutters or shutter counts; this is a camera body metric.

claims.claim: no fungus or scratch on the lens
claims.evidence: Photo 1 shows the front element but is not clear enough to rule out internal fungus or fine scratches.
Lenses are passive or powered by the camera; they do not use independent batteries or chargers.

risks.proof: A video showing the lens successfully focusing on near and far objects.
A clear photo looking through the lens elements with a bright light shone from the other side.

risks.risk: Incompatible mount (e.g., Nikon or Sigma mount instead of Canon)
risks.proof: A clear photo of the rear metal mount of the lens.
risks.if_unproven: as the least valuable mount variant

proof_requests: Photo of the rear mount to confirm it is for Canon EF.
Video of the lens performing autofocus on a camera.
Photo of the glass elements with a light behind them to check for fungus.
Clarification on why the description mentions a shutter count and battery for a lens.
response.reason: The seller's description is for a camera (mentioning shutter count, battery, and charger) while the photos are of a lens. This total mismatch between text and item is a primary indicator of a fraudulent listing or a scammer using stolen photos.
